chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If the servant stands for salat (prayer) and then makes his prayer light, Allah, the Exalted, says to His angels: “Do you not see My servant? It is as though he sees that the fulfillment of his needs is in the hand of other than Me. Does he not know that the fulfillment of his needs is in My hand?”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act of worship being discussed
key_terms.بِيَدِ غَيْرِي: in the hand of other than Me, meaning attributed to someone besides Allah
key_terms.بِيَدِي: in My hand, meaning under Allah’s sole power and control
key_terms.فَخَفَّفَ: he made it light, meaning he performed it hastily or without due fullness
key_terms.قَضَاءَ: fulfillment or completion, here referring to the granting of needs
key_terms.مَلَائِكَتِهِ: His angels, before whom Allah addresses this servant’s state

ai.seo_question: What does it mean if a person rushes through salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that rushing and making salat (prayer) too light reflects a spiritual heedlessness toward Allah, the Exalted. It reminds the believer that all needs are fulfilled only by Allah, so salat should be performed with presence, reverence, and reliance upon Him.
